# Native and Version Contract Checklist: Native egui Adapter and Versioned Contracts

**Purpose**: Review whether the S039 requirements completely and unambiguously define native adapter semantics, independent versioning, integrity, recovery, and scope boundaries
**Created**: 2026-09-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are all governed inputs and generated native outputs named without leaving ownership implicit? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001 to FR-003]
- [x] CHK002 Are logical units, density, text scaling, interaction targets, and invalid-transform behavior all covered? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK003 Are supported, adapted, unsupported, and pending-proof capability states defined for both renderer and host ownership? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK004 Are all independent version identities and their applicable records specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009 to FR-012]
- [x] CHK005 Are integrity, exact-source provenance, compatibility, failure, and recovery requirements all present? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013 to FR-020]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is the native adapter boundary clear enough to prevent browser-source emulation and a general cross-renderer language? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK007 Is the distinction between renderer support, host supply, and evidence status unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK008 Are version meaning, ownership, compatibility scope, and change classes explicitly required rather than implied by version strings? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK009 Is deliberate adoption clearly distinguished from generation compatibility and publication availability? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017 to FR-019]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Do native semantic-traceability requirements agree with the independent-version requirements? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, FR-009 to FR-013]
- [x] CHK011 Do exact recovery and fail-closed integrity requirements agree across manifests, release records, adapter artifacts, and guidance? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012 to FR-020]
- [x] CHK012 Do production rebuild requirements preserve the source/artifact boundary and approved identity constraints? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016, FR-021]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [x] CHK013 Are primary native generation, version evaluation, pinned recovery, incompatibility, and tamper scenarios represented by acceptance criteria? [Coverage, User Stories 1 to 3]
- [x] CHK014 Are invalid transforms, unsupported recipe semantics, partial native support, and missing optional tooling addressed? [Coverage, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK015 Are missing, ambiguous, mismatched, and silently changed release artifacts covered as failure scenarios? [Coverage, Edge Cases, Spec §FR-014 to FR-020]

## Non-Functional and Boundary Requirements

- [x] CHK016 Are accessibility, identity preservation, minimum runtime compatibility, and full verification expectations explicit? [Coverage, Spec §FR-016, FR-023, SC-005, SC-008]
- [x] CHK017 Are committed generated output, synthetic fixture publication, release publication, consumer mutation, and full conformance explicitly excluded? [Boundary, Spec §FR-021 to FR-022]
- [x] CHK018 Can every success criterion be measured without silently treating native fixture readiness as downstream adoption? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001 to SC-008, Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
